intelligence.description: 1Password provides password management, secrets protection, and identity-security tools for individuals, developers, and businesses.
company: 1Password began as a consumer password manager and expanded into security products for teams and enterprises. Its platform helps users store credentials and sensitive information while giving organizations controls over access, secrets, and shared accounts.

The company announced a $620 million Series C in January 2022 at a $6.8 billion valuation. Its private-market relevance comes from the broader shift from standalone password tools to identity-security platforms embedded in daily employee and developer workflows.
intelligence.why_it_matters: 1Password is a read-through for private cybersecurity and identity-software demand. Its ability to move from consumer trust into enterprise deployments illustrates how security products can broaden into recurring business-software platforms.

changed.text: 1Password is founded as a password-management product.
A Series B financing values the company at $2B.
The company announces $620M of Series C funding at a $6.8B valuation.

takeaways: 1Password's value rests on trusted daily use and expansion into broader identity-security workflows.
The $6.8B figure is the last reported priced valuation and should not be interpreted as a current market price.
Enterprise adoption can deepen retention but also increases competition with large security suites.
Secrets management and developer workflows are important opportunities beyond consumer password storage.
